defs_parts: Eight labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Video only: the term comes from the course's film skills and assignment briefs.
Outside source: the term comes from a source outside the course text.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A beat sheet lists every beat's picture, words and seconds, in order.
A shot is one take, and the route is the whole path.
A route check measures speed, turn rate, roll and height on every frame.
A fixed frame rate gives every frame the same slice of game time.
Resolution is pixels in one frame, and frame rate is frames per second.
Every claim in the narration needs evidence on screen.
bookends.segment: Name The Film Term, Defend It
bookends.command: Quiz me on walkthrough film terms with short cases from filming a game I built, one at a time. Use beat sheet, storyboard, shot, route, waypoint, real-time capture, render, fixed frame rate, resolution and b-roll. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is about filming a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.

skin_warnings: NO RENDERABLE BEATS: no beat carries a shot.remotion.pattern or Manim annotation — the pipeline will render NOTHING and every slot becomes a YOU-slate. The sheet was authored without the scene contract.
